title.en: Neural system and the human neural system

hook.en: You touch a hot vessel in the kitchen and pull your hand back before you even feel the pain. Messages race along your nerves faster than you can think.
hook.kn: ಅಡುಗೆಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿಸಿ ಪಾತ್ರೆ ಮುಟ್ಟಿದಾಗ ನೋವು ತಿಳಿಯುವ ಮೊದಲೇ ಕೈ ಹಿಂದೆಳೆಯುತ್ತೀರಿ. ನರಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಸಂದೇಶಗಳು ಯೋಚನೆಗಿಂತ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಓಡುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Coordination is the process through which two or more organs interact and complement each other's functions. During exercise, for example, muscles need more energy and oxygen, so the rates of respiration and heartbeat rise and blood flow increases. The neural system and the endocrine system together coordinate and integrate all activities of organs. The neural system provides an organised network of point-to-point connections for quick coordination; the endocrine system provides chemical integration through hormones. The neural system of all animals is made of highly specialised cells called neurons, which detect, receive and transmit stimuli. In lower invertebrates like Hydra it is a network of neurons; in insects it has a brain and a number of ganglia and neural tissues; vertebrates have a more developed neural system.
body.kn: ಎರಡು ಅಥವಾ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಅಂಗಗಳು ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಕಾರ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಪೂರಕಗೊಳಿಸುವುದೇ ಸಮನ್ವಯ. ನರವ್ಯೂಹ ವೇಗದ ಸಮನ್ವಯ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ, ಅಂತಃಸ್ರಾವಕ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಹಾರ್ಮೋನುಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ರಾಸಾಯನಿಕ ಸಮನ್ವಯ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೈಡ್ರಾದಲ್ಲಿ ನರಕೋಶಗಳ ಜಾಲ, ಕೀಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಿದುಳು ಮತ್ತು ನರಗಂಟುಗಳಿವೆ.

narration.en: The teacher maps the human neural system into CNS and PNS with its divisions, and shows coordination during exercise.

say.en: The neural system has two parts: the central neural system, which processes information, and the peripheral neural system, the nerves.
Peripheral fibres are afferent, carrying impulses to the CNS, or efferent, carrying orders out from it.
The PNS has a somatic part to the skeletal muscles and an autonomic part to involuntary organs. The autonomic part splits into sympathetic and parasympathetic.
Neural coordination is quick and point to point; hormonal coordination is slower but reaches every cell. During exercise both work together.

explanation.en: The peripheral neural system (all nerves) has afferent fibres carrying impulses to the CNS and efferent fibres carrying them out. Its efferent part is divided into the somatic and the autonomic neural systems.

title.en: Divisions of the human neural system

body.en: The human neural system has two parts. The central neural system (CNS) includes the brain and the spinal cord and is the site of information processing and control. The peripheral neural system (PNS) comprises all the nerves of the body associated with the CNS. Nerve fibres of the PNS are of two types: afferent fibres transmit impulses from tissues and organs to the CNS, and efferent fibres carry regulatory impulses from the CNS to the peripheral tissues and organs. The PNS is divided into the somatic neural system, which relays impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles, and the autonomic neural system, which transmits impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles. The autonomic neural system is further divided into the sympathetic and parasympathetic neural systems. The visceral nervous system is the part of the PNS that supports the viscera.
body.kn: ಮಿದುಳು ಮತ್ತು ಮಿದುಳು ಬಳ್ಳಿ ಕೇಂದ್ರ ನರವ್ಯೂಹ (CNS). ದೇಹದ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ನರಗಳು ಪರಿಧಿಯ ನರವ್ಯೂಹ (PNS). ಅಭಿವಾಹಿ ತಂತುಗಳು CNS ಗೆ, ಅಪವಾಹಿ ತಂತುಗಳು CNS ನಿಂದ ಸಂದೇಶ ಒಯ್ಯುತ್ತವೆ. PNS ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾಯಿಕ ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ವಾಯತ್ತ ನರವ್ಯೂಹಗಳು; ಸ್ವಾಯತ್ತ ನರವ್ಯೂಹದಲ್ಲಿ ಅನುವೇದನಾ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಾನುವೇದನಾ ಭಾಗಗಳು.

points.en: Afferent: to the CNS; efferent: from the CNS
Somatic → skeletal muscles; autonomic → involuntary organs and smooth muscles

problem.en: Classify each nerve pathway: (a) a signal from a skin pain receptor travelling to the spinal cord; (b) a signal from the spinal cord to the biceps; (c) a signal from the CNS that speeds up the heart.

steps.en: (a) It carries an impulse from a tissue to the CNS — an afferent fibre of the PNS.
(b) It carries an impulse from the CNS to a skeletal muscle — efferent, somatic neural system.
(c) It carries an impulse from the CNS to an involuntary organ — efferent, autonomic neural system (sympathetic division).
